name: Garments of the Light

meta.previous: In Favor of the Light (Dun Morogh)
chain: In Favor of the Light (Dun Morogh)

summary: At Maxan Anvol’s urging, you go south of Kharanos to help a wounded mountaineer before you receive the Garments of the Light.

sections.title: An Urgent Trial
sections.body: Maxan Anvol, the priest trainer, asks for practical aid before ceremony. Acolytes usually face formal trials to prove they deserve church vestments. But Mountaineer Dolf is wounded, and he needs help now.

sections.title: Aiding the Mountaineers
sections.body: South of Kharanos, you find Mountaineer Dolf wounded in the line of duty. Restorative prayers mend his injuries. Power Word: Fortitude strengthens him and helps keep an Ironforge defender alive.

sections.title: Robes of the Church
sections.body: Once Dolf has received aid, Maxan Anvol presents you with formal garments. The robes give warmth against Dun Morogh’s chill and mark you as a servant of the Light. You are ready to aid wounded wanderers and local guards.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this quest?
faq.answer: Maxan Anvol tests whether a novice priest can use early spells to help someone in need. You find the injured Mountaineer Dolf south of Kharanos, heal his wounds, and strengthen him with Power Word: Fortitude.
Maxan Anvol is the dwarven priest trainer in Kharanos. He mentors young priests arriving from Coldridge Valley and favors the Light’s direct work of saving lives over strict formal liturgy.
Dolf is an Ironforge mountaineer stationed near Kharanos, injured on patrol. He waits south of the settlement, where initiates are sent to mend his wounds and grant him Fortitude.

faq.q: Why does a priest receive specific garments for this task?
faq.answer: Vestments and robes show a practitioner’s devotion and rank within the Holy Light. Soldiers and other community members can recognize a robed priest who can tend life-threatening injuries and offer spiritual guidance.

faq.q: Why do dwarves worship the Holy Light?
aliases: do dwarves believe in the light
faq.answer: The dwarves of Ironforge adopted the Holy Light through centuries of close cultural exchange and alliance with the humans of Lordaeron and Stormwind. Dwarven priests join traditional highland grit with reverence for compassion, tenacity, and protection.

faq.q: What happens after completing this trial?
aliases: what comes after garments of the light
faq.answer: After the trial, Maxan Anvol encourages the newly vested acolyte to venture out, practice combat and support spells, and test their limits alongside other travelers. Harder trials within the church await as the priest grows in experience and power.

angles.text: As a priest, you move from novice to recognized minister of the Holy Light, trusted to keep companions alive on the front lines.
As a dwarf, you know Ironforge mountaineers guard Dun Morogh’s dangerous passes. Tending wounded scouts like Dolf strengthens the bond between dwarven faith and military defense.
As an Alliance member, you look to the Holy Light for comfort and battlefield healing while soldiers hold the line against troggs, beasts, and worse.
